differences.native: MySQL isolates the current word with SUBSTRING_INDEX, validates it with REGEXP, and appends each converted character with CONCAT.
differences.app: SQLite isolates the same word with SUBSTR and INSTR, checks the same one-hyphen ASCII-letter grammar with LENGTH, REPLACE, and GLOB, and appends with ||.
differences.rationale: SQLite lacks SUBSTRING_INDEX, the required REGEXP operator, and CONCAT. Both queries retain the same character-by-character recursive state, word-start updates, capitalization decisions, terminal row, projection, and ordering.
